works.title: Freedom and Socialism/Uhuru na Ujamaa
works.author: Julius Nyerere
works.description: Essays developing Ujamaa as African socialism rooted in traditional communal values.
works.significance: Blueprint for African socialism; influenced continent-wide

works.title: Return to the Source: Selected Speeches of Amilcar Cabral
works.author: Amilcar Cabral
works.description: Cabral's speeches on national liberation, culture, and revolutionary theory.
works.significance: Assassinated 1973; Africa's Gramsci; 'claim no easy victories'

works.title: Revolution in Guinea: An African People's Struggle
works.author: Amilcar Cabral
works.description: Cabral's analysis of Guinea-Bissau's liberation struggle against Portuguese colonialism.
works.significance: Practical revolutionary theory from armed struggle

works.title: Ma Rainey's Black Bottom
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play set in 1927 Chicago recording studio exploring tensions between blues musicians and white management.
works.significance: First play of Pittsburgh Cycle; Chadwick Boseman's final film

works.title: Fences
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play about Troy Maxson, former Negro League player, and his strained family relationships in 1950s Pittsburgh.
works.significance: Pulitzer Prize; Tony Award; Denzel Washington film

works.title: Joe Turner's Come and Gone
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play set in 1911 Pittsburgh boarding house where former slave searches for his wife.
works.significance: New York Drama Critics' Circle Award

works.title: The Piano Lesson
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play about siblings fighting over family piano carved with their ancestry during slavery.
works.significance: Pulitzer Prize; Samuel L. Jackson film 2024

works.title: Two Trains Running
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play set in 1969 Pittsburgh diner during Black Power era, examining community and change.
works.significance: Tony Award nomination; explores late Civil Rights era

works.title: Seven Guitars
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play about blues guitarist Floyd Barton's final days in 1948 Pittsburgh.
works.significance: New York Drama Critics' Circle Award

works.title: King Hedley II
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play about ex-con trying to rebuild life in 1985 Pittsburgh Hill District.
works.significance: Continues character from Seven Guitars; Reagan-era urban blight

works.title: Gem of the Ocean
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play set in 1904 about 285-year-old Aunt Ester and her spiritual cleansing of troubled man.
works.significance: First chronologically in Cycle; Aunt Ester embodies African-American soul

works.title: Radio Golf
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Final play of Cycle about Black mayoral candidate and gentrification in 1990s Pittsburgh.
works.significance: Wilson's final play; completed weeks before his death

works.title: Jitney
works.author: August Wilson
works.description: Play about unlicensed cab drivers in 1970s Pittsburgh facing urban renewal displacement.
works.significance: First written of Cycle; Tony Award for Best Revival 2017

works.title: Babel-17
works.author: Samuel R. Delany
works.description: Novel about poet who must decode alien language that may be weapon, exploring how language shapes thought.
works.significance: Nebula Award; pioneering Black queer science fiction

works.title: Dhalgren
works.author: Samuel R. Delany
works.description: Massive experimental novel set in mysterious American city cut off from world.
works.significance: Sold million copies; polarizing masterpiece of experimental SF

works.title: Nova
works.author: Samuel R. Delany
works.description: Space opera about quest for rare element in dying star, exploring mythology and economics.
works.significance: Proto-cyberpunk; Black protagonist in far future

works.title: Essential Essays, Volume 1: Foundations of Cultural Studies
works.author: Stuart Hall
works.description: Collection of Hall's foundational essays on culture, class, representation, and politics.
works.significance: Father of Cultural Studies; shaped the entire field

works.title: Essential Essays, Volume 2: Identity and Diaspora
works.author: Stuart Hall
works.description: Essays on race, identity, diaspora, and representation including 'Cultural Identity and Diaspora'.
works.significance: Most influential theorist of Black British identity

works.title: Encoding and Decoding in the Television Discourse
works.author: Stuart Hall
works.description: Essay arguing audiences actively decode media messages rather than passively receiving them.
works.significance: Revolutionized media studies; reception theory cornerstone

works.title: In My Father's House: Africa in the Philosophy of Culture
works.author: Kwame Anthony Appiah
works.description: Philosophical exploration of African identity and critique of racial essentialism.
works.significance: Herskovitz Prize; Anisfield-Wolf Award; cosmopolitan African philosophy

works.title: Cosmopolitanism: Ethics in a World of Strangers
works.author: Kwame Anthony Appiah
works.description: Argument for cosmopolitan ethics balancing universal moral concern with respect for difference.
works.significance: Major work in global ethics; 'universality plus difference'

works.title: A Dying Colonialism
works.author: Frantz Fanon
works.description: Analysis of Algerian revolution's social transformations including role of women and radio.
works.significance: Revolutionary praxis in action; shows colonialism's death throes

works.title: Toward the African Revolution
works.author: Frantz Fanon
works.description: Posthumous collection of political essays on Algeria, Africa, and decolonization.
works.significance: Completes Fanon's revolutionary thought; died at 36

works.title: The African Origin of Civilization: Myth or Reality
works.author: Cheikh Anta Diop
works.description: Evidence that ancient Egypt was Black African civilization challenging Eurocentric historiography.
works.significance: With Du Bois, greatest influence on 20th century Black thought; Dakar 1966

works.title: Civilization or Barbarism: An Authentic Anthropology
works.author: Cheikh Anta Diop
works.description: Comprehensive synthesis of Diop's arguments for African origins of civilization.
works.significance: Diop's masterwork; reclaims African history

works.title: Precolonial Black Africa
works.author: Cheikh Anta Diop
works.description: Comparative study of political and social systems in precolonial Africa.
works.significance: Proves sophistication of African political systems before colonialism

works.title: The Mis-Education of the Negro
works.author: Carter G. Woodson
works.description: Critique of American education system's failure to teach Black history and its psychological effects.
works.significance: Founded Black History Month; 'Father of Black History'

works.title: Notebook of a Return to the Native Land
works.author: Aimé Césaire
works.description: Long surrealist poem about returning to Martinique, coining 'négritude' and celebrating Black identity.
works.significance: Birth of Negritude movement; Césaire co-founded with Senghor

works.title: Discourse on Colonialism
works.author: Aimé Césaire
works.description: Poetic essay arguing colonialism dehumanizes both colonizer and colonized, comparing it to Nazism.
works.significance: 'Declaration of war' on colonialism; foundational postcolonial text

works.title: A Tempest
works.author: Aimé Césaire
works.description: Adaptation of Shakespeare's Tempest from Caliban's perspective as colonized subject.
works.significance: Postcolonial reimagining; Caliban as freedom fighter

works.title: Revolutionary Suicide
works.author: Huey P. Newton
works.description: Newton's autobiography explaining Black Panther Party philosophy and his political evolution.
works.significance: Black Panther co-founder; revolutionary autobiography

works.title: Seize the Time: The Story of the Black Panther Party
works.author: Bobby Seale
works.description: Seale's account of founding Black Panthers, written while imprisoned.
works.significance: Primary source on Black Panther Party founding; staple of Black Power literature

works.title: Assata: An Autobiography
works.author: Assata Shakur
works.description: Shakur's account of her life, Black Liberation Army membership, and escape to Cuba.
works.significance: First woman on FBI's most wanted terrorists list; still in Cuba

works.title: Black Power: The Politics of Liberation
works.author: Stokely Carmichael (Kwame Ture) and Charles V. Hamilton
works.description: Manifesto defining Black Power as political and economic self-determination for Black communities.
works.significance: Coined institutional racism; Black Power movement manifesto

works.title: The Philadelphia Negro
works.author: W.E.B. Du Bois
works.description: Pioneering sociological study of African-American community in Philadelphia's Seventh Ward.
works.significance: First scientific sociological study of Black community in America

works.title: Darkwater: Voices from Within the Veil
works.author: W.E.B. Du Bois
works.description: Essays, sketches, and poems on race, gender, and labor including famous 'The Souls of White Folk'.
works.significance: More radical than Souls of Black Folk; critiques white supremacy

works.title: The Gift of Black Folk
works.author: W.E.B. Du Bois
works.description: Argument for African-American contributions to American civilization.
works.significance: Reclaims Black contributions to America; counter-narrative

works.title: Abuja Treaty: Treaty Establishing the African Economic Community
works.author: African Union
works.description: Treaty creating framework for African economic integration and eventual common market.
works.significance: Foundation for African Continental Free Trade Area

works.title: Constitutive Act of the African Union
works.author: African Union
works.description: Founding document of African Union establishing principles and objectives of continental organization.
works.significance: Foundation of modern pan-African governance

works.title: Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area
works.author: African Union
works.description: Treaty creating world's largest free trade area by number of countries, connecting 1.3 billion people.
works.significance: Largest free trade area after WTO; African economic integration

works.title: Morning Yet on Creation Day
works.author: Chinua Achebe
works.description: Essays on African literature defending it against Western critical standards and colonialist perspectives.
works.significance: Achebe's literary criticism; challenges colonialist critics

works.title: Hopes and Impediments: Selected Essays
works.author: Chinua Achebe
works.description: Essays including famous critique of Conrad's Heart of Darkness as racist.
works.significance: 'Image of Africa' essay challenged Western canon; paradigm shift

works.title: The Old Drift
works.author: Namwali Serpell
works.description: Multigenerational epic spanning Zambian history through three families over century.
works.significance: Arthur C. Clarke Award; Anisfield-Wolf Book Award; Harvard professor

works.title: Stay With Me
works.author: Ayobami Adebayo
works.description: Novel about Nigerian couple's marriage tested by infertility and family pressure.
works.significance: Wellcome Book Prize; debut novel; new Nigerian literature wave

works.title: A Spell of Good Things
works.author: Ayobami Adebayo
works.description: Novel weaving together two Nigerian families across class divides during economic crisis.
works.significance: Dylan Thomas Prize; masterful second novel

works.title: We Need New Names
works.author: NoViolet Bulawayo
works.description: Novel about girl growing up in Zimbabwean shantytown who immigrates to America.
works.significance: Man Booker Prize shortlist; debut novel; Zimbabwean emigration

works.title: Glory
works.author: NoViolet Bulawayo
works.description: Animal Farm-style allegory of Mugabe's fall in Zimbabwe using animal characters.
works.significance: Booker Prize longlist; political satire of Zimbabwean authoritarianism

works.title: An Unkindness of Ghosts
works.author: Rivers Solomon
works.description: Generation ship novel where Black passengers live in lower decks under plantation-like conditions.
works.significance: Afrofuturist; reimagines slavery in space; non-binary protagonist

works.title: The Deep
works.author: Rivers Solomon
works.description: Novella about underwater people descended from pregnant African women thrown from slave ships.
works.significance: Based on clipping. song; Lambda Literary Award

Caribbean.note: Caribbean writers exploring colonialism, identity, and creolization

Diaspora.note: Works by authors of African descent writing from outside the continent, including African-American canon, Harlem Renaissance, civil rights literature

Pre-colonial Oral Traditions.description: Traditional folktales, myths, and oral narratives
Pre-colonial Oral Traditions.note: Represented through collections like Tales of Amadou Koumba and works incorporating oral tradition

Negritude.description: Literary and ideological movement of French-speaking Black intellectuals

Harlem Renaissance.description: African-American cultural movement centered in Harlem, New York featuring Hughes, Hurston, Toomer, Cullen, McKay, Larsen
